title: Prediction markets you can't call after the fact

changes.text: Stream peak markets used to stay open for 30 minutes after a stream started, long enough to watch the viewer count pass the line and then bet on it. They now open before a scheduled stream and close 15 minutes before it's due, or the moment it goes live if it starts early. If a bet ever lands after the real start, that market voids and everyone gets their money back.

Fewer automatic markets, so the bets are in one place: one Top gainer a day on the Lunch tick and up to five stream peaks a day, one per talent, on the busiest talents. The "Up on the tick?" calls are off for now, because a tick usually moves the same way as the one before it, which made them too easy to call.
Stream peak lines now sit within 5% of the talent's median. Rounding could put a smaller channel's line a third below it, which made YES nearly free.

A voided market now undoes everything. If you sold for more than you paid and the market later voids, that gain goes back along with everyone else's refunds, and a voided market no longer moves you on the forecasters board.
